editorial:
Imagine getting a letter from a loved one who is passing away, only to find out they want you to bike 450 miles across Northern California. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a group of people who didn't really get along but are now forced to ride together for a charity cause. The movie feels like a road trip on wheels, capturing the beauty of the coast and the messy emotions of people dealing with grief. It is a slow burn that focuses more on the conversations and the bonding between the characters than on the sport of cycling itself.

The acting feels very natural, and you will find yourself rooting for the group to finish the ride despite their arguments. While the pace is a bit slow in the middle, the payoff at the end makes it worth your time. If you are in the mood for a heartwarming story about family and second chances, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: As the group reaches the final mile, they discover that the dying man left secret letters for each person to read at specific landmarks. These letters reveal a hidden family secret that explains why he wanted them all together. They finally forgive each other and cross the finish line as a united family. The movie ends with them visiting the man's grave, feeling a sense of peace and true connection for the first time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family healing and beautiful scenery.
